A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RTO research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained theory and relocated summarization experiments.

before.justification: V2 reports original Pythia-2.8B alignment experiments on HH-RLHF and TL;DR, including GPT-4 comparisons, reward evaluations, temperature analyses, and training curves.

after.justification: V3 reports original Llama-3-8B benchmark and ablation experiments, while retaining the original TL;DR results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: V2 optimizes DPO-derived token rewards plus KL regularization. V3 Equation (4.7) adds a separately trained sentence-level reward, weighted by beta3 and assigned to the final token. This additional reward model and terminal signal materially change practical RTO, although its DPO-to-PPO framework remains.

E1.justification: The HH-RLHF helpful-dialogue experiments are removed. V3 adds UltraFeedback preference training and conversational instruction-following evaluation on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard. Reddit TL;DR summarization remains in Appendix E rather than being newly added or removed.

E2.justification: V3 Table 1 newly evaluates R-DPO, SimPO, and TDPO alongside SFT, DPO, and PPO. Figure 3 adds Semi-RTO and RS-PPO ablation comparators. The retained TL;DR comparison still includes SFT, DPO, PPO, and DPPO.

E3.justification: The new main study uses Llama-3-8B, 2048-token training, length-controlled and style-controlled win rates, and benchmark-specific decoding. It specifies an 8B PPO reward model and a 1B auxiliary RTO reward model/critic, and introduces data-fraction evaluations. The earlier HH-RLHF evaluation protocol disappears; TL;DR's 100-prompt GPT-4-0613 protocol is retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds token-versus-sentence-versus-terminal reward granularity tests, an RS-PPO control isolating reward shaping, and a data-efficiency study in Figures 3–4. HH-RLHF temperature and training-curve analyses are removed. The corresponding TL;DR analyses are retained as Figures 5–6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables and curves continue the existing practice of reporting results without quantified experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: HH-RLHF results are removed, while v3 Table 1 newly reports RTO/PPO scores of 27.00/19.47 on AlpacaEval 2 LC and 20.3/16.2 on Arena-Hard SC, plus new ablation and scaling findings. These are new experimental settings, not matched-setting improvements over v2. TL;DR results remain unchanged, including RTO's 61% win rate against DPO.

T1.justification: Equation (4.7) revises the formal practical reward definition, accompanied by a new coefficient-rescaling argument. The MDP formulation, assumptions, Proposition 3.2, Theorem 4.2, and mathematical material in Appendices A–C remain unchanged; no new guarantee or proof establishes the added reward component.

C1.justification: The central MDP formulation, DPO-plus-PPO method, and provable sample-efficiency contributions remain. V3 adds a headline empirical claim of matching PPO with approximately one-eighth of the data and continuing to improve after PPO saturates, while making benchmark-specific performance claims explicit in the abstract.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly attributes RTO's advantage primarily to reward shaping rather than the aggregate DPO reward. Section 4.2 also explains the additional sentence reward as protection against extreme response lengths and argues that a smaller critic can offset the added computational cost.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code/model availability statement and link. Appendix D documents checkpoints, dataset variants, optimizer scheduling, PPO stabilization, decoding settings, eight 80GB A100 GPUs, and memory-saving techniques for the new study. HH-RLHF implementation details disappear, while TL;DR configurations and evaluation instructions are retained in Appendix E.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 expands its concurrent-work discussion to TDPO and SimPO and discusses subsequent implicit-reward work by Cui et al. and Yin et al. References also change with the datasets, benchmarks, and implementation. This is a focused update that preserves the main distinction from prior preference-learning approaches.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized from separate setup/results sections into benchmark results followed by mechanism analyses. Summarization material is consolidated into new Appendix E, and Appendix D is rewritten around implementation. The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion are also revised.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially rebuilt with a new benchmark table, an ablation table captioned Figure 3, and a new three-panel Figure 4. HH-RLHF displays are removed; the TL;DR matrix and plots are relocated and resized as Table 2 and Figures 5–6. Figures 1–2 remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens empirical validation through verbosity-controlled benchmarks, broader baseline comparisons, and controls that investigate reward shaping and data efficiency. These address v2's limited evidence about why RTO works, while Appendix D materially improves reproducibility. Removing HH-RLHF evidence reduces continuity, and naming/cross-reference inconsistencies remain, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger experimental support and implementation guidance.
